Article Title: ‘Will contest at least 150 seats in UP’: Congress discusses alliance talks with SP
Article Text:
SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: The Congress will contest at least 150 seats in the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections early next year, a party leader said on Monday, asserting that the Congress is “entitled” to contest half the seats in its alliance with the Samajwadi Party (SP).Seat-sharing talks with the SP are likely to be finalised in October, according to Rajendra Pal Gautam, the Congress’ Uttar Pradesh in-charge.“Seat-sharing will likely be finalised in October. Congress has candidates available to contest all 403 seats. Under the alliance, the Congress is entitled to 50% of the seats. We will not contest fewer than 150 seats,” Gautam told ANI.“For the last two months, Congress has been working on seat-sharing in Uttar Pradesh. Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi, KC Venugopal and I are looking after this work,” he added.The Congress and the SP are key constituents of the Opposition INDIA bloc in Uttar Pradesh. The two parties contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in the state as alliance partners, winning 43 of the 80 seats. The SP won 37 seats — its best performance in a Lok Sabha election — while the Congress secured six. The BJP, which rules both the Centre and the state, finished second with 33 seats, down from 62 in 2019.The previous SP-Congress alliance in Uttar Pradesh, for the 2017 assembly elections, was less successful. The SP won 47 seats and was voted out of power, while the Congress secured only seven seats.
Article Summary: The congress will contest at least 150 seats in the uttar pradesh assembly elections early next year, a party leader said on monday. Rajendra pal gautam, the congress’ uttar pradesh in-charge, said seat-sharing talks with the samajwadi party (sp) are likely to be finalised in october.

Article Title: ‘Speaker fully cognisant of three-month time-frame’: SC on Mamata faction plea against 10 rebel TMC MLAs
Article Text:
SC on disqualification petitions against 10 rebel TMC MLAs

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday said it has "every reason to believe" that the West Bengal assembly Speaker is "fully cognisant" of an order fixing a three-month time frame to decide petitions seeking disqualification of MLAs.The observations came from a bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana during the hearing of a plea filed by Sohandeb Chattopadhyay, a senior MLA of the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress (TMC) faction.Chattopadhyay had approached West Bengal assembly Speaker Rathin Bose on July 7, seeking the disqualification of 10 MLAs of the rebel group on the grounds that they had “acted against the party’s interests."“We have every reason to believe that the speaker is fully cognisant of the decision of this court and he will make an endeavour to take an appropriate decision within the time-frame fixed,” PTI quoted the bench as saying. The bench was referring to a January 2020 Supreme Court order that set a three-month timeline for the-then Manipur assembly Speaker to decide a disqualification petition.“In this case, the three-month period would expire on October 10,” the bench added before disposing of the plea.The Supreme Court’s observations came days after the West Bengal assembly secretariat issued notices to the 10 MLAs aligned with the rebel TMC camp, seeking their replies within a week to a disqualification petition filed by the Mamata Banerjee-led faction.In his petition, Chattopadhyay sought directions for the Speaker to expeditiously decide the disqualification petition filed against the 10 legislators, including Ritabrata Banerjee, the leader of the opposition in the West Bengal assembly.Besides Ritabrata Banerjee, the notices were issued to Arup Roy, Firhad Hakim, Sandipan Saha, Akhruzzaman Ansari, Shiuli Saha, Sabina Yasmin, Biplab Mitra, Javed Khan and Rathin Ghosh.The TMC split following the West Bengal assembly elections in April, when the party was voted out of power after 15 years, paving the way for the BJP to form its first government in the state.The rebel faction claims to have the support of 65 of the 80 Trinamool MLAs elected in the polls.The confrontation has also spilled over into Parliament, with 20 Lok Sabha MPs aligned with the rebels quitting the TMC and joining the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), which has declared its support for the BJP-led NDA government at the Centre.
Article Summary: Sc on disqualification petitions against 10 rebel tmc mlas in west bengal. Supreme court says it has "every reason to believe" that the west bengal assembly speaker is "fully cognisant" of an order fixing a three-month time frame to decide petitions seeking disqualification of mlas.

Article Title: SC stays Bombay HC order of bail to Ramesh Mhatre
Article Text:
Shiv Sena municipal corporator Ramesh Mhatre. (Photo: ANI)

MUMBAI: Supreme Court on Monday stays the bail granted recently by Bombay high court to Shiv Sena municipal corporator Ramesh Mhatre,73, in a case of assault on civic hospital doctors and warned that members of the medical fraternity cannot be assaulted at will in such a manner.The SC directed him to surrender within three days.A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta were hearing a bail cancellation plea of The Maharashtra government which challenge the HC order ofThe bench orally cited the general and larger implications an assault on doctors in the medical fraternity. “Medical fraternity serves the people. They cannot be attacked in this manner,” the bench said.Appearing for Mhatre, senior counsel Siddharth Dave said for bail cancellation a higher standard was required. He pointed out that trial was underway before a Magistrate with two prosecution witnesses having deposed and a woman doctor to depose on October 3.Mhatre cooperated with the probe and trial the SC was informed.The maximum sentence under the law is five years’ imprisonment for the main offence in the case and there was no obstruction caused in the trial caused, Mhatre’s counsel also submitted.While acknowledging the concerns raised by the bench, the counsel submitted that as a “criminal case” evidence had to form the basis of the outcome.The State had referred to Mhatre’s antecedents while seeking cancellation of his bail.Dave, submitted that Mhatre had been acquitted in 18 of the 19 cases cited against him. “Call for the records of those cases also,” the Court immediately said.The SC had on September 7 concerns over the cases of assaults on doctors and hospital staff in Maharashtra and said they cannot be treated as routine law-and-order.The Bombay HC bench led by then Acting Chief Justice RV Ghuge had taken the matter suo motu observing the seriousness of the assaults. And on July 27 in its initial order come down on Mhatre and the police and Justice Ghuge had noted that Mhatre was arrested 48 hours after the alleged assault. “Why do you (Mhatre) behave like this? Why beat the public? They are your voters. Surprising that a person who goes to voters and says ‘vote for me, I want to serve you’. ..after winning, starts beating people,” he said while hearing pleas filed by the corporator and others seeking bail on any stringent condition HC deemed fit. “Even in public life, you are for the public, are here for the public.”On August 7 the Bombay HC had fast tracked their trial and granted bail to Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre and three others accused behind bars in the July 6 assault on doctors including a woman doctor at a municipal hospital in Dombivli, but all four were to remain outside Maharashtra till the criminal trial begins.The HC had also framed a time-line for probe and prosecution to proceed swiftly and the time to be spent outside Maharashtra for all four would likely be a month.The endevour should be to complete trial in 3 months once charge is framed, the HC said.The ACJ Ghuge dictating the order in open court had said, “In a democracy an elected representative is by the people and for the people. If the elected representative is accused of assaulting his own voters, such a situation is bound to dent the fabric of democracy in this country and erode public confidence.’’Police arrested Mhatre on July 8 for allegedly slapping and punching a doctor and assaulting a resident medical officer. A local court granted him bail on July 14, while he was in a hospital. He was released but on July 18 the HC took up the matter suo motu and staying the bail order for all four, directed Mhatre to surrender. He did on July 19.
Article Summary: Shiv sena municipal corporator ramesh mhatre,73, in a case of assault on civic hospital doctors. Supreme court on monday stays the bail granted recently by bombay high court to shiv sena corporator. The bench orally cited the general and larger implications an assault on doctors in the medical fraternity.

Article Title: Stone pelting, tear gas and clashes with police: What is happening in Ujjain
Article Text:
The demolition is part of a larger road-widening exercise in Ujjain.

What happened at the site

Road widening for Simhastha

Ujjain prepares for 2028 gathering

NEW DELHI: Tensions rose in Ujjain on Monday as protesters clashed with police during demonstrations over development work in the city. Police were deployed in large numbers around the Shahi Masjid Complex as sporadic protests and stone pelting were reported in the area.The clashes erupted after the demolition of a portion of the Shahi Masjid as part of a road-widening project. The work is linked to preparations for the Simhastha Kumbh Mela in 2028, with authorities planning a major infrastructure overhaul ahead of the religious gathering.Police used tear gas shells to control a crowd in the city as stone pelting occurred when a large group of people clashed with them at the spot where a portion of Shahi Masjid was planned to be demolished.Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel has been deployed at the spot.SP Pradeep Sharma says, "...all communities and sections of society are continuously extending their cooperation and support in their respective areas. Even today, the demolition work, initiated by the mosque committee itself, is underway at the Shahi Masjid. As a precautionary measure, a full security perimeter has been established, and entry is prohibited for everyone.However, certain miscreants attempted to create a disturbance and resorted to stone-pelting. The police personnel present at the scene responded by using tear gas and mild force to disperse the crowd. Leaders from the Muslim community are also issuing video messages urging calm... The situation is now fully under control. The demolition work by the mosque committee is continuing steadily...""We had anticipated this and conducted thorough briefings and multiple meetings to discuss every aspect. It is precisely because of this planning that we cleared the entire Chhatri Chowk area; there is no crowd here now, and a global security perimeter is in place. Some police personnel sustained minor injuries during the stone-pelting incident, but they remain alert and ready for duty," he said.The officer futher said: "We utilized tear gas to manage the situation. The entire area is being monitored via CCTV and drones. We have also been keeping a close watch on social media. Individuals who came from outside the district to incite trouble were detained by the police at the border late last night and have been taken into custody at various police stations. We will now identify the perpetrators using CCTV and drone footage and register FIRs against those found involved. An attempt to block the road was also made by some women; however, after being counseled and shown video footage of the situation, they withdrew the blockade. The road is open. I appeal to everyone to please cooperate; if anyone engages in such activities, strict action will be taken against them. As you can all see, this entire undertaking is being carried out by the committee itself, with everyone's consent."Protesters tried to move through narrow lanes towards the area, with some women seen being pushed forward as the crowd attempted to proceed. Stones were also thrown at police personnel deployed to maintain order.The situation remained tense as security forces stayed at the spot to prevent further escalation.Congress MP Imran Pratapgarhi, meanwhile, criticised the demolition and urged the Madhya Pradesh government to take public sentiment into account."The administrative efforts to demolish the Ujjain Shahi Masjid under the pretext of road widening should be a bit more sensitive. Demolishing a 600-year-old heritage site just for road widening and development in the name of progress is the height of hatred. It has come to my notice that when the matter is pending in court, what message does the administration intend to send by repeatedly laying siege to the masjid? Thousands of youth in Ujjain are continuously raising their voices on this issue. My request to the Ujjain administration is to respect public sentiments and acquire the necessary land for road widening from the other side. Demolishing such a historically significant heritage site cannot be considered a normal event under any circumstances," the Congress MP said.The demolition is part of a larger road-widening exercise in Ujjain. Authorities have identified 272 structures for demolition as preparations intensify for the 2028 Simhastha gathering.Earlier, chief minister Mohan Yadav had participated in demolition work at his ancestral home. He said giving up the property had been emotionally difficult but was necessary for the wider development project."This is the place where I grew up, playing and running around, and now I am stepping forward to dismantle it with my own hands. It certainly has an emotional impact. However, if it is necessary for the administration and essential for the Simhastha, then this sacrifice must be made. I am satisfied that we are all doing this together," he said.Yadav said his decision was also intended to encourage other residents affected by the project to cooperate with the administration."The entire state and the country are watching this. People are demolishing their homes willingly and happily, dedicating themselves to the cause so that others may benefit greatly," he said.Ujjain Municipal Corporation chairperson Kalawati Yadav said preparations for Simhastha include several major infrastructure projects. The event is held once every 12 years on the banks of the Shipra River and is expected to draw millions of devotees."In 2028, Ujjain will host the Simhastha Mela, one of the world's largest spiritual gatherings, held every 12 years on the banks of the Shipra River. Extensive preparations are underway, including around 29 kilometres of new ghats, a diversion project, dams and other infrastructure works to improve the city. With millions of devotees expected, road widening has become essential," she said.The road-widening project is part of the wider redevelopment plan aimed at improving Ujjain's infrastructure and handling the expected influx of pilgrims during the 2028 Simhastha Mela.
Article Summary: Police used tear gas shells to control a crowd in the city as stone pelting occurred. Clashes erupted after the demolition of a portion of the shahi masjid as part of a road-widening project. The work is linked to preparations for the simhastha kumbh mela in 2028. The demolition is part of a larger road-widening exercise in ujjain.

Article Title: 'Medical fraternity cannot be touched': SC cancels Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre's bail in doctor assault case
Article Text:
SC cancels Mhatre’s bail in doctor assault case, stays Bombay HC order

The Supreme Court has cancelled the bail granted by the Bombay High Court to Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre, who is accused of assaulting a doctor at a civic hospital. The court also stayed the High Court order granting him bail on a plea filed by the Maharashtra government.While cancelling Mhatre’s bail, the Supreme Court said the message should go “loud and clear” that the medical fraternity cannot be touched.A court in Maharashtra had framed charges against Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre and four others over the assault of doctors, including a female doctor, and nurses at Dombivli’s Shastri Nagar Municipal Hospital following a dispute over the treatment of a pregnant woman on July 6.Mhatre, along with Pramod Nikam, Ramesh Pawar, Akshay Karande and Sadhana Karande, appeared before Fast-Track Court Judge N P Vasade two days after police filed a 1,832-page chargesheet in the case.The accused have been charged under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to assault and causing hurt, assaulting or obstructing a public servant, unlawful assembly and rioting, common intention, criminal intimidation and intentional insult, besides offences relating to the dignity or modesty of a woman.They have also been booked under Sections 3 and 4 of the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act and Sections 37(1)(3) and 135 of the Maharashtra Police Act for allegedly violating orders imposed to maintain public order.Mhatre had been staying in Goa after the Bombay High Court granted him conditional bail in August. The High Court had directed him to remain outside Maharashtra until the chargesheet was filed and ordered that the trial be fast-tracked for completion within three months.After the chargesheet was filed, the condition ceased to operate, following which Mhatre returned to his residence and appeared before the court earlier this month.
Article Summary: Sc cancels mhatre’s bail in doctor assault case, stays bombay hc order. Shiv sena corporator is accused of assaulting a doctor at a civic hospital. The court also stayed the high court order granting him bail on a plea filed by the maharashtra government.

Article Title: SIR row: Nadda backs EC, sends message to Rahul Gandhi and opposition
Article Text:
Nadda​ accused the oppn of repeatedly raising allegations despite responses from the Election Commission.

Kharge demands CEC's resignation

Rahul Gandhi's allegations over SIR

NEW DELHI: Union minister JP Nadda on Monday attacked the opposition and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over the SIR row surrounding the Election Commission , saying, “repeating a lie a hundred times does not make it the truth”.Nadda also targeted Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind Kejriwal, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, accusing them of attempting to “malign and weaken” the country's autonomous and constitutional institutions.Speaking to reporters, Nadda took a direct aim at the Congress leader saying, “Rahul Gandhi, listen carefully: repeating a lie a hundred times does not make it the truth; the truth cannot be defeated.”“For Rahul Gandhi, Arvind Kejriwal, Akhilesh Yadav, and Mamata Banerjee, the sole agenda has become to malign and weaken the nation's autonomous and constitutional institutions. This is the same 'toolkit mentality' that hatches a new conspiracy every morning to stall the country's development: level allegations, disrupt the national atmosphere, and flee. This has become the opposition's modus operandi,” he said.“They care nothing for national security, public welfare, or the country's honor and prestige. Their only objective is to seize power, not to serve the people, but to nurture dynastic politics and reap personal benefits... The public has taught a befitting lesson to the forces seeking to create instability in the country in the past, and in the future too; every delusion and conspiracy of theirs will be shattered in the court of the people,” he added.Nadda further accused the opposition of continuing to raise allegations despite the Election Commission’s responses, saying it was attempting to create confusion and disrupt the atmosphere in the country.“Today, as the nation realizes the resolve of a 'Viksit Bharat' (Developed India) through the tireless efforts of its 1.4 billion citizens, and as India’s influence resonates across the global stage, the Congress and the entire 'INDI Alliance' are, unfortunately, frustrated and despondent at this progress..." Nadda said."Lacking policies and a vision, they are now devising new ploys to spread confusion and anarchy across the country. We all witnessed the uproar created nationwide just a few days ago over a fabricated story. Now, even after the Election Commission has exposed every lie they propagated, they are once again attempting to vitiate the atmosphere,” Nadda added.He alleged that Rahul and Kejriwal “make allegations and walk away; they have nothing to do with public interest.”The Union minister further accused the opposition of attempting to create confusion and disturb the atmosphere in the country despite lacking “intent and vision”.“We saw a few days ago how an attempt was made to disturb the atmosphere across the country on the basis of a fabricated news report. Now, even after all members of the Election Commission have responded to their allegations, they are once again engaged in efforts to vitiate the atmosphere in the country,” Nadda said.Nadda also contrasted the BJP 's approach to power with that of the opposition, saying, “For BJP, power is a means to serve the interests of 140 crore people.”He said the BJP's objective was to serve citizens and fulfil its commitment to Antyodaya, while accusing the Opposition of seeking power for dynastic politics and its own interests.Nadda's remarks came after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and other leaders demanded the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and alleged that he was propagating the BJP's philosophy.“They will say like this only, but their own people have exposed them, and their own people are telling. Even a Chief Secretary of Kerala says, our CEC himself told him to contest the election. It means that a person who is in the highest position is propagating the BJP’s philosophy, and he has become a BJP worker. So it is clear. There is nothing. He should resign. If he has got any little moral right, he should resign from that post. And afterwards, we have to take action against him, even after resignation,” Kharge said.“I have called a working committee meeting for tomorrow, and there we'll discuss; all the working committee members will give their suggestions. And we are going to fight seriously. This issue concerns the entire country, the existence of our democracy, and the country's survival. That's why we are very serious about this issue. We'll fight, and we'll see that,” he added.The political row comes amid opposition criticism of the Election Commission's handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Rahul Gandhi had earlier alleged that the 2024 Lok Sabha and assembly elections were “all rigged” and demanded the immediate resignation of Gyanesh Kumar.He also accused the CEC of “match-fixing elections”, citing a news channel report claiming that Kumar had approached former Kerala chief secretary Jiji Thomson to contest the 2026 Assembly elections on a BJP ticket.The Election Commission, meanwhile, clarified that a letter sent to the Cabinet Secretary that had drawn scrutiny related to the functioning of an officer on deputation to the poll body and not to any policy matter.The row also follows an Indian Express report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months on decisions and orders related to SIR and other electoral matters. The reported objections included issues concerning Form 6, voter deletions and access to electoral-roll databases.The poll body rejected the suggestion that these objections amounted to institutional dissent over final decisions, saying operational queries, inputs and suggestions raised during the draft stage were part of its standard administrative and decision-making process.The Election Commission maintained that all decisions taken by it, including those related to SIR, were unanimous and had the approval of all three commissioners, PTI reported.Opposition parties, including the Congress, CPI, CPI(M), Trinamool Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT), have demanded Kumar's resignation.Meanwhile, CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya said an INDIA bloc meeting is expected on September 30 to discuss the SIR exercise and the functioning of the Election Commission.
Article Summary: Nadda​ accused the oppn of repeatedly raising allegations despite responses from the election commission. Nadda also targeted aam aadmi party chief arvind kejriwal, samajwadi party chief akhilesh yadav and former west bengal chief minister mamata banerjee.

Article Title: Bank unions call off 3-day strike after assurances, IBA to study demands
Article Text:
Bank unions withdraw three-day strike after late-night agreement with IBA on key demands.

NEW DELHI: Bank unions called off their proposed three-day strike just before midnight after the Indian Banks Association agreed to look into their demands."A high-level committee of IBA and UFBU (United Forum of Bank Unions) will be formed immediately to deliberate on the issue of declaring the remaining Saturdays as holidays. This committee will explore, all possible alternatives; discuss with all stakeholders, and work out a solution acceptable to all stakeholders and, more importantly, the customers," a late night communication said.Unions want a five-day work week, which is being resisted by banks as it may inconvenience customers.The late-night announcement came after what turned out to be a working Sunday for state-run bank employees as govt ordered branches to stay open so that customers are not inconvenienced.
Article Summary: Bank unions withdraw three-day strike after late-night agreement with iba on key demands. Indian banks association agreed to look into their demands. Unions want a five-day work week, which is being resisted by banks as it may inconvenience customers.

Article Title: UP man held in Pakistan spying case freed after 22 years
Article Text:
Agra court clears Jhansi man in 2004 spy case

A man from Jhansi , who was accused of being part of a Pakistan spy network in 2004 and spent a year in jail, has been acquitted by an Agra court due to "insufficient evidence". Jameel Ahmad, 50, out on bail, faced charges of cheating and criminal conspiracy. Implicated by two suspected Pak agents in police custody, Ahmad was in 2004 held with what cops claimed was a CD holding "sensitive military info". Court said the prosecution failed to prove his involvement and highlighted that the CD, a key evidence, was found broken into pieces when produced on record.
Article Summary: Agra court clears jhansi man in 2004 spy case. Jameel ahmad, 50, out on bail, faced charges of cheating and criminal conspiracy. Ahmad was in 2004 held with what cops claimed was a cd holding "sensitive military info"

Article Title: Watch: Landslide blocks Kedarnath route in Rudraprayag’s Chirbasa, over 1,500 pilgrims evacuated
Article Text:
Kedarnath route blocked by landslide in Rudraprayag's Chirbasa village

Joint teams complete rescue operation

NEW DELHI: Around 1,500 pilgrims stranded on the Kedarnath route near Chirbasa were safely rescued and escorted to Gaurikund after a landslide blocked the route late Sunday night, officials said.The pilgrims were stranded around three kilometres from Gaurikund after a landslide hit the route near Chirbasa, news agency ANI reported.The Rudraprayag District Control Room (DCR) informed Sonprayag Police about the situation late on September 27, following which the SDRF Sonprayag team, led by Sub-Inspector Ashish Dimri, rushed to the spot.Prioritising the safety of the pilgrims, the rescue teams carefully assisted them across the affected stretch. Around 1,500 pilgrims were brought safely to the other side of the landslide zone and escorted towards Gaurikund.The operation was carried out despite continued rockfall and the risk of further landslides in the area. Rescue personnel coordinated the movement of pilgrims to ensure they crossed the dangerous stretch safely.The coordinated efforts of the SDRF, NDRF and DDRF helped ensure that all the stranded pilgrims were safely evacuated from the affected area.Officials said the rescue operation was successfully completed despite the challenging conditions at the site.
Article Summary: Around 1,500 pilgrims stranded on the kedarnath route near chirbasa. Rescue teams carefully assisted them across the affected stretch. The operation was carried out despite continued rockfall and the risk of further landslides in the area.

Rape claim, campus unrest and midnight clashes: What happened at LPU

Rape case registered, SIT formed

NEW DELHI: Students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara went on a rampage on Sunday, vandalising property and blocking NH-44 during protests over claims that an outsider raped a female student on the university campus. The protests later turned violent as students clashed with police, damaged and set fire to vehicles, and pelted stones at security personnel. Several policemen were injured.The university has suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed mid-term examinations until further notice. Heavy police deployment has been made on the campus, while students have started leaving for their homes.Classes suspended, exams postponedFollowing the violence, LPU suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed mid-term examinations until further notice.The administration appealed to students to remain calm, follow official instructions and stay connected for further updates.Several rounds of talks between protesting students and the university management remained inconclusive.Vice Chancellor Sandhu assured students that their genuine grievances would be addressed.The protesters demanded that LPU Founder-Chancellor Ashok Mittal, who is also a BJP Rajya Sabha MP, visit the protest site and assure them that their concerns would be resolved. They also sought that access to the University Management System not be blocked and that students not be victimised for participating in the protest.A large police force led by ADGP M F Farooqui entered the LPU campus after the violence escalated. More than 2,000 personnel have been deployed to maintain security through the night, Farooqui said.“We will ensure security on the campus throughout the night... A force of over 2,000 personnel is currently deployed here. Law and order has been fully maintained and restored... The process is ongoing, and we are working to keep the situation under control. I cannot provide further details at this moment. To the families whose daughters are staying in the hostel here: please do not worry; everyone is safe... The atmosphere here is completely calm, and the university students are also cooperating with us in restoring peace. ..,” he said.Jalandhar Police Commissioner Satinder Singh said reports of disturbances in the hostels were rumours and that all hostels had been checked.“First of all, reports of disturbances in the hostels were merely rumours. All hostels have been checked, and there are no issues. Traffic has resumed, and the situation is normal. Other matters will be resolved through discussions with the students... Overall, the atmosphere is fine, and any minor issues will be addressed... Please inform the families that all students are safe and there is no cause for concern,” Singh said.DIG (Jalandhar Range) Naveen Singla also said the situation had been brought under control and that traffic movement on NH-44 would soon be restored.Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has directed strict action against those responsible for the unrest at Lovely Professional University (LPU), the Chief Minister’s Office said.Mann also directed Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav to visit the spot and assess the situation.The protest began near Girls' Hostel-3 around 1 am on Sunday after students alleged that a female student had been raped by a plumber three days earlier. They also claimed the hostel warden had been informed but no action was taken.The protesters blocked NH-44 outside the university from around 8 am, causing long queues of stranded vehicles. Police later attempted to clear the blockade, but students allegedly threw water bottles at them and clashed with personnel.Police resorted to a mild lathi charge, following which students moved towards the campus and continued to pelt stones at police vehicles. Two police vehicles were set on fire, while four to five vehicles were damaged, according to Jalandhar Rural SSP Harvinder Singh Virk.Viral videos showed damaged property, vehicles and an ATM kiosk on the campus. Some students were also seen climbing onto a decommissioned MiG-23UM aircraft and a military tank installed on the premises.A truck driver, Vikas Yadav, said, “We have been stranded since 7 AM; there is no sign of things opening up yet... We are extremely distressed... We have had to abandon our vehicles and flee...”Police said an FIR had been registered against an unknown person based on a complaint by the students and a special investigation team had been formed.Singla said the girl was staying in Hostel No. 3 and had returned to her home after students alleged that no action had been taken on the matter. He said the investigation would involve student representatives.“We will analyse forensic samples, CCTV camera footage, call records, etc., before reaching a conclusion,” Singla said.The DIG also said students had demanded that the hostel staff comprise only women, adding that the management would address the demand.Asked about another death, Singla said a female student from Telangana studying at LPU had died by suicide 15 days earlier. “If the students say that there was foul play, action will be taken,” he said.LPU Vice Chancellor Jaspal Singh Sandhu said the university was not aware of any such rape incident but would cooperate with the investigation.LPU management has denied the rape allegations, with Registrar Monica Gulati saying certain “anti-social elements” were spreading “false, baseless and fabricated” claims.The university released a video featuring three female students identified as residents of Room No. 504 of the hostel. In the video, the students said no rape had taken place in their room and asked police and other students not to disturb them.Gulati introduced the video by saying, “I would like you to hear what the girls residing in room number 504 of GH3 told us.”The first student said, “So, we are the residents of room number 504. Nothing of that sort happened in our room; we have been living here for the past two months. Please, police and students, do not bother us. Nothing like that happened in our room, and we are not involved in this at all.”The second student said, “We have been extremely distressed today, and if we face further trouble, we will involve our parents. Please do not harass us.”The third added, “And the police should also stop coming to our room repeatedly; otherwise, we will call our parents.”Gulati later said, “The only conclusion to be drawn from all this is that anti-social elements and individuals with vested interests are behind this.”The opposition Congress criticised the AAP government over the law and order situation in Punjab.“What is happening at LPU is deeply concerning. If students have serious questions or concerns about any incident, they deserve transparent, impartial and time-bound answers, not rumours or suppression. The violence is a testament to the failed law and order situation in Punjab,” state Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring said.“NH-44 has been blocked since the morning, yet not a single representative from the AAP government has bothered to meet the students and hear their grievances,” Warring said.
Article Summary: Students of lovely professional university (lpu) in punjab’s phagwara went on a rampage on sunday. They vandalised property and blocked nh-44 during protests over claims that an outsider raped a female student on the university campus. The protests later turned violent as students clashed with police, damaged and set fire to vehicles, and pelted stones at security personnel.

Article Title: 12 BJP CMs defend EC amid SIR row, hit back at Rahul Gandhi after poll body's fresh note
Article Text:

What BJP CMs said

Rahul Gandhi’s cryptic post

The controversy

NEW DELHI: A dozen BJP chief ministers held press conferences in their respective states on Sunday, a day after the Election Commission of India (ECI) issued a press release responding to a media report that had claimed a “rift” between Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.According to a statement issued by the ruling party, the chief ministers accused Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and his party-led opposition INDIA bloc of “conspiring to defame constitutional institutions."In states where the BJP or its NDA allies are not in power, state BJP presidents or leaders of the opposition from the saffron party addressed media instead.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis remarked that "no vote was stolen, Rahul Gandhi's mind was stolen." He accused the Lok Sabha leader of opposition of "seeking to spread anarchy by defaming institutions" while claiming to defend the Constitution.Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath accused the opposition parties of creating "confusion" over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. In Assam, Himanta Biswa Sarma described the INDIA bloc as an “alliance of losers,” while Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary argued that "cleansing" the voter list was necessary because “booth capturing no longer works in the country.”West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari pointed to the Congress’s support for the SIR in Keralam, where it won, and its opposition to the exercise in Bengal after losing the election.Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami objected to what he described as an "attempt to defame institutions by presenting a note from an internal discussion as a final decision.”Rajasthan chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma questioned why the Congress had not "verified the facts" before making serious allegations over the June 24, 2025, orders concerning the nationwide SIR, which he maintained were adopted by the ECI full consensus of the CEC and the election commissioners.Chhattisgarh's Vishnu Deo Sai accused the Congress of resorting to “anti-national” conduct after “having lost more than 100 elections.” Referring to the Election Commissioners’ joint statement, accompanied by a photograph of the three officials seated at a table, Sai argued that it had exposed what he called a “conspiracy to tarnish the country’s image.”Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta, where a third of the electorate was removed and a third of those remaining received notices as part of the ongoing revision, framed the Opposition’s position on the issue as an attempt to “divert attention from its failures."Rahul Gandhi, meanwhile, posted cryptically on X: “I love swimming in the sea when it’s rough. It teaches you that rough is just another kind of calm.”At a press conference on September 24, a day after The Indian Express published its report, the Congress leader claimed his “vote chori” (vote theft) allegation stood “vindicated.” The Raebareli MP also demanded that CEC Gyanesh Kumar resign or be removed, accusing him of “treason.”The Indian Express reported on September 23 that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected to at least 14 decisions over 10 months concerning the ongoing SIR exercise and related matters.The ECI has not disputed that objections were raised; however it characterised them as "disagreements" that were subsequently resolved, stressing that the final decisions were "unanimous." While Sandhu and Joshi are yet to speak to the media, the poll panel's press note second statement outlined several measures and clarifications.The BJP has maintained that the ECI’s press notes have “settled the matter”. Its allies, who, like the opposition, had sought an explanation from the poll body, also welcomed the commission's statement.
Article Summary: The election commission of india (eci) issued a press release responding to a media report that had claimed a “rift” between chief election commissioner (cec) gyanesh kumar and the two election commissioners. The indian express reported on september 23 that election commissioners sukhbir singh sandhu and vivek joshi had objected to at least 14 decisions over 10 months.

Article Title: 'Left' in existential crisis: From CPI-CPM rift in Kerala to Delhi rout, old fault lines deepen
Article Text:
The Left faces a deeper political challenge as electoral setbacks, internal tensions and shrinking influence converge

Pinarayi probe: Another challenge after Kerala defeat

DUSU polls: Why isn't Left mobilisation becoming votes?

CPI vs CPM: When opposition itself becomes a battlefield

From Bengal to Kerala: How did the Left reach here?

Poll Vote & Share your view How pivotal is the recent defeat in Kerala for the future of the Left in India? Extremely pivotal Moderately pivotal Not very pivotal Not pivotal at all 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What next for the Left?

There was a time when the Left’s political footprint stretched from West Bengal to Tripura and Kerala. Its influence travelled further still, through trade unions, university campuses, farmers’ movements and a cadre network that kept the red flag visible even where Communist parties were not in power. That map has steadily grown smaller.For India’s Left, the question is no longer only about shrinking electoral numbers. It is increasingly about where the Communist movement still has the political space, organisational confidence and social influence to assert itself. In Delhi, the SFI-AISA alliance has struggled to translate visible participation in student mobilisations into votes. In Kerala, the two principal constituents of the Left Democratic Front, the CPM and CPI, have found themselves publicly at odds over even the distribution of positions within the opposition, and that too after a heavy defeat in the assembly elections.These may appear to be separate battles, but they have come at a particularly difficult moment for the Left. The Kerala defeat has left it without a state government, the CPM and CPI are publicly disagreeing over the way forward, former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan is facing a probe, and the Delhi university results have again exposed the gap between the Left’s visibility in student movements and its electoral reach.The timing makes these developments particularly significant. The Left’s retreat has been a long process. The fall of the Left Front in West Bengal in 2011, the loss of Tripura in 2018 and the steady decline in its parliamentary strength had already reduced the Communist parties’ national footprint. Kerala had remained the exception, a state where the Left retained a durable organisational network and, in 2021, even broke the state’s established cycle of alternating between the LDF and UDF governments. Its defeat in 2026 means that India currently has no state government led by a Communist party.But the more revealing question may be what is happening beneath the election results. Is the Left merely going through another electoral trough, particularly after a decade in power in Kerala, or are the latest developments exposing older fault lines, from leadership and alliance tensions to the difficulty of converting traditional political mobilisation into electoral support?On September 22, the UDF government ordered a police inquiry based on an Enforcement Directorate report concerning allegations involving former chief minister and current leader of opposition Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter Veena T and son-in-law PA Mohammed Riyas in the CMRL-Exalogic case. The state government said the inquiry would be entrusted to the state police; reports said it would initially be conducted by the Crime Branch without registration of an FIR.The underlying allegations are already part of an ED investigation. The agency has alleged financial irregularities involving payments made by Cochin Minerals and Rutile Ltd to Veena's now-defunct company Exalogic Solutions, and has sought action against Vijayan and others. The Kerala government's decision followed legal advice on whether the information and material supplied by the ED warranted a preliminary inquiry.For the CPM, however, the political dimension is inseparable from the legal one. Party general secretary MA Baby has said the party will fight the matter “legally and politically”, while accusing central agencies of having been used against opposition leaders.That places the Left in an unfamiliar position in Kerala. For a decade, Vijayan and the CPM were operating from government. Now the former chief minister is leading the opposition while facing a probe ordered by the government that replaced him.The probe comes only months after the LDF lost power following a decade in government, at a time when the CPM is already examining what went wrong and trying to regroup in opposition. The question is therefore not simply whether the allegations withstand investigation. The episode also puts Vijayan and the record of the previous government back under scrutiny at a particularly difficult moment for the party.The Delhi University Students' Union election offers a different window into the Left's problem, particularly its ability to convert activism and issue-based mobilisation into electoral support.The SFI-AISA alliance had been visible in campaigns around issues including student housing, examinations and accountability, and had participated prominently in the CJP mobilisation. Yet its electoral numbers declined in three of the four central-panel contests compared with 2025. Its presidential candidate Ananya Raturi received 5,377 votes, almost identical to the 5,385 polled by the alliance's candidate last year. But its vice-presidential tally fell from 4,163 to 2,383, the secretary vote from 9,535 to 8,734 and the joint-secretary vote from 8,425 to 5,837.The results also showed that student politics cannot simply be read as a binary contest between the major national parties and the Left. ABVP won three of the four central-panel positions, while Independent candidate Deepanshu Shokeen won the vice-president's post with 30,615 votes. He had previously been associated with Congress-affiliated NSUI but contested independently after not receiving its ticket.For the Left, the striking element is the gap between mobilisation and electoral conversion. A political organisation can be prominent in protests, articulate grievances on campuses and participate in wider movements, but that visibility does not automatically translate into votes.The presidential contest is particularly revealing. The Left candidate finished with 5,377 votes, while ABVP's Yash Dabas won with 24,576 and NSUI's Vijay Shankar Meena polled 22,523. The result does not erase the Left's presence on campus, but it does expose the difficulty of turning that presence into control of student institutions.And that is why the DUSU result matters beyond one university election. Student politics has historically been an important space for the Left to recruit, organise and build its next generation of political workers. Sitaram Yechury, for instance, rose through student politics at JNU before eventually becoming CPI(M) general secretary.The question for the Left now is simpler: if it can still bring young people to protests and movements, why is it struggling to bring them to the ballot box?The strain is also visible inside Kerala's Left alliance. After the LDF's assembly defeat, the CPI demanded the post of deputy leader of the opposition in the assembly, arguing for a larger role within the alliance. The CPM, however, rejected the demand, with Vijayan publicly opposing it.On the surface, the disagreement is about a post. But underneath it is a larger debate about how the LDF should function after its election defeat. The CPI has argued for greater sharing of responsibilities and “collective leadership”, while the CPM has maintained that the alliance should follow its established conventions.The disagreement soon spilled into public. CPI state secretary Binoy Viswam criticised Vijayan's stand, while senior CPI leader C Divakaran went further and questioned Vijayan's authority to dismiss the demand. Divakaran also argued that Vijayan should have taken responsibility for the election defeat rather than becoming leader of the opposition.The CPM pushed back too. CPM state secretariat member C N Mohanan questioned the CPI's electoral strength and accused it of using pressure tactics against the larger ally.The dispute may appear procedural because the deputy leader's post is largely an organisational and parliamentary position. But its political significance lies elsewhere. The CPI has sought greater recognition after the LDF's defeat, while the CPM, as the dominant force in the alliance, remains the principal party responsible for its direction.The two parties have since tried to prevent the dispute from escalating further. But the episode illustrates a problem that often becomes sharper after an electoral defeat: who takes responsibility for the loss, and who gets to decide the course correction?Kerala's 2026 verdict completed a long retreat. West Bengal's Left Front had ruled continuously from 1977 until 2011, while Tripura remained under Left Front rule for 25 years before the BJP ended that run in 2018. Kerala subsequently became the Left's last major governing base.But the story of the Left's decline has not been the same everywhere. In West Bengal, the 2011 defeat ended 34 years of uninterrupted Left Front rule and the Communist parties have since struggled to recover their old electoral space. In Tripura, the BJP displaced the Left after 25 years in power and emerged as its principal rival. Kerala followed a different trajectory, with power traditionally alternating between the LDF and Congress-led UDF.That is what made the LDF's 2021 victory particularly significant. The Vijayan government returned for a second consecutive term, breaking Kerala's four-decade pattern of alternating governments and giving the Left something it no longer had elsewhere: a state where it could demonstrate that it remained capable not only of surviving, but of retaining power.The 2026 defeat is therefore different from Bengal and Tripura and cannot automatically be equated with the organisational collapse witnessed elsewhere. Yet the scale of the setback raises questions beyond normal anti-incumbency. The LDF was reduced from 94 seats to 35, while the UDF won 102. The CPI(M) also suffered defeats in areas traditionally associated with its organisation, including parts of Kannur. BJP candidates won three seats, Chathannoor, Nemom and Kazhakoottam, including constituencies that had been held by LDF leaders.The larger national trajectory has been just as stark. At its parliamentary peak in 2004, the Left parties together had 59 Lok Sabha MPs and provided crucial outside support to the first UPA government. Twenty-two years later, their presence in Parliament and across state governments is a fraction of what it was.The decline cannot be traced to a single election or a single cause. The Left has had to contend with the loss of old strongholds, changes in the nature of work and organised labour, the rise of powerful regional parties, the BJP's expansion into states where the Left once had substantial space, and the challenge of reaching a generation of voters with little memory of the Communist parties at the height of their political influence.Kerala had, for years, stood apart from that national decline. The 2026 result does not mean the Left's organisational base in the state has disappeared, but it has removed its last seat of state power and made the problems elsewhere much harder to ignore.With no Communist-led state government left, a diminished parliamentary presence, weaker conversion of student mobilisation into votes and visible friction among its own principal parties, the Left finds itself at one of its most difficult political moments.The challenge is no longer simply how to win the next election. It is whether the political space that once made the Communist movement a national force can still be reconstructed, and whether the Left can address its old fault lines while finding its place in a changing political landscape.
Article Summary: The left faces a deeper political challenge as electoral setbacks, internal tensions and shrinking influence converge. The kerala defeat has left it without a state government, the cpm and cpi are publicly disagreeing over the way forward, and former chief minister pinarayi vijayan is facing a probe.

Article Title: PM Modi pens tribute to Ashok Singhal: 'A great personality who was committed to nation-building'
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

There is a beautiful saying that the tree does not consume its own fruit, nor does the river retain its waters. Both exist for the benefit of others. Our saints and seers have long taught us that a life devoted to the welfare of those around us acquires a meaning far greater than individual achievement. If there is one person in whom this spirit was constantly reflected, it was Shri Ashok Singhal ji.Starting Sept 27, we mark his birth centenary to celebrate an outstanding personality who brought together spiritual pursuit, cultural awakening and decades of dedicated organisational work.I consider it a privilege that I had innumerable opportunities to interact with Ashok ji and receive his affection. One of the earliest instances dates back to 1981, when I was a young karyakarta going about the organisational duties given to me. I received a handwritten letter from him. Naturally, it was a noteworthy moment for me. He talked about an important upcoming programme and gave a few tasks to be done.Over several decades, I saw him work day and night. He would undertake long and often difficult travels to the remotest of areas. He was particularly passionate about travelling across tribal areas of Gujarat. His mind was constantly running, thinking about what more one can do for those on the margins of society.Whenever any part of the nation was affected by a natural disaster, Ashok ji was either among the first to reach there himself or among those guiding karyakartas to help those affected. My own experience with him in the aftermath of the 2001 Kutch earthquake was unforgettable.This spirit of compassion and care for others is something that came to Ashok ji very early in his life. He hailed from a very illustrious and prosperous family. His father, Shri Mahavir ji, was a distinguished administrator. One of his bro-thers, Shri BP Singhal ji, went on to become a police officer and later a member of Parliament. Another brother, Shri VP Singhal ji, was the chief secretary of Tripura when the state was just formed. Other family members succeeded in the world of commerce and agriculture. But from a young age, Ashok ji was attracted to something else altogether... the revival of Bharat and bringing glory to Maa Bharti's children.Growing up in Prayagraj, Ashok ji would sit for hours on the banks of the Sangam. The river naturally interested him, but so did the people who came, such as saints, seers and devotees. It nurtured an understanding of India's cultural ethos and strengthened his intention to do something for society. This desire to live for others drew him to RSS. He embraced every responsibility that came his way with enthusiasm, discipline and a sense of duty.Ashok ji nurtured institutions and movements through persistence and hard work. He was blessed with a formidable voice and an oratory that could hold an entire gathering in its spell. Equally noteworthy was his care for fellow karyakartas. Anyone who came into contact with him could not help but marvel at his remarkable simplicity. He shared a deep bond with Sant Samaj and commanded immense respect among saints and seers across the country. They valued his counsel and listened to him with great regard.My mind goes back to two instances which brought out the legendary persona of Shri Ashok Singhal ji. The first was in 1993, when Vishwa Hindu Parishad organised a convention in US to mark 100 years since Swami Vivekananda's Chicago address. The vision to host such a conference overseas, the planning and the bringing together of diverse stakeholders revealed the organisational genius of Ashok ji.The second instance is from 2000. World Hindu Conference was organised in Port of Spain in Trinidad and Tobago. I could see how his presence ignited so much enthusiasm among other delegates. After my address, his words of appreciation were a very moving experience for me. I saw yet again how his encouragement filled every karyakarta with so much energy.No mention of Shri Ashok Singhal ji is complete without recalling his pivotal role in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. Who can forget his address at Boat Club Rally in 1991? Or the defining image of an injured and bleeding Ashok ji at the peak of the movement. Today, if there is a grand Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, it is because of stalwarts like him who selflessly immersed themselves in the effort to make it possible. He would have been the happiest person on seeing Ram Mandir take shape in Ayodhya.Shri Ashok Singhal ji was blessed with remarkable clarity of thought and one area wh-ere it was clearly seen was his belief that our society needs to be harmonious, that the message of brotherhood has to be reaffirmed. He worked towards strengthening social unity and equality. He firmly believed that there could be no distinction of any kind in society and that every individual deserved equal dignity and respect. It was his thought that the first brick of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya would be laid by Shri Kameshwar Choupal Ji, a grassroots VHP karyakarta from Bihar who hailed from the marginalised sections of society. At a dharm sansad in Kashi, he decided that the Dom Raja would be honoured and went on to work with him as part of various community efforts.Beyond nation-building, Ashok ji had two areas that were very close to his heart: education (especially Vedic education) and music. As the MP from Varanasi, I feel very proud that the city I represent, the eternal Kashi, has played its part in Ashok ji's life. He was educated at BHU and was also known to be a good student. He was closely associated with the Ekal Vidyalaya initiative, which worked to extend basic education to remote villages, especially among tribal communities.He was a voracious reader as well as a good listener, and he always told younger karyakartas to read as much as possible.Those who knew Ashok ji closely knew how well he sang. I recall meetings in Nagpur, where he would sing the Ekal Geet, leaving everyone mesmerised and setting the tone for the meeting. A video of him surprising everyone and singing 'Yeh Matru Bhumi Meri, Yeh Pitra Bhumi Meri' during his 90th birthday celebrations in 2015 went viral.On his birth centenary, let us ensure that more youngsters know about his greatness. And let us renew our pledge to realise his dreams for our nation and our people.
Article Summary: Shri ashok singhal ji brought together spiritual pursuit, cultural awakening and decades of dedicated organisational work. He would undertake long and often difficult travels to the remotest of areas. Anyone who came into contact with him could not help but marvel at his remarkable simplicity.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring. Vijay held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore. It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas.Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. Scheme draws on tamil tradition of ‘thaimaaman seer’ the scheme has retrospective effect from june 22, vijay’s birthday.tamil nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, according to nfhs-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.

Article Title: Satya Niketan PG collapse: Owner seeks bail citing medical condition; court lists hearing for Sept 30
Article Text:

Owners failed to take safety precautions

NEW DELHI: Delhi’s Satya Niketan's owner on Monday has sought regular bail, citing his age and medical condition, with the Patiala House Court issuing notice on the plea.The court has also sought a medical report from the jail authorities before taking up the matter on September 30, news agency ANI reported.Owner Hari Ram Gupta is an accused in the September 6 collapse of the five-storey PG building in Satya Niketan that killed seven people. His earlier bail plea was rejected by the court, which observed that the investigation was still at an initial stage and the chargesheet had not yet been filed.The court also took note of the deaths, injuries and the fact that one victim was still critical at the time.In a status report filed before the Delhi High Court earlier, Delhi Police said the building owners failed to take adequate safety precautions during construction and repair work, allegedly creating a situation that endangered the lives of PG residents.Police said the building owner Urmila Gupta, her husband Hari Ram Gupta and their son Mahesh Gupta jointly managed the property. The police report also alleged that the premises were being used commercially without obtaining the required land-use conversion permission.Meanwhile, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has launched a major enforcement drive following the collapse.According to a compliance affidavit filed before the Delhi High Court, MCD demolished 543 properties and sealed 178 others for unauthorised construction between September 6 and September 23. It also issued 354 show-cause notices, including 205 sealing notices, and passed 98 demolition orders during the 17-day period.MCD said Property No. 14 in Satya Niketan, which collapsed, had never had a sanctioned building plan approved by the civic body.
Article Summary: Hari ram gupta is an accused in the september 6 collapse of the five-storey pg building in satya niketan. His earlier bail plea was rejected by the court, which observed that the investigation was still at an initial stage and the chargesheet had not yet been filed.

Article Title: Lung cancer deaths down 16% with low-dose CT screening: IARC
Article Text:
Lung cancer deaths can be reduced through low-dose CT screening, which can also help detect the disease before it reaches advanced stages in people at high risk, according to an IARC assessment.

NEW DELHI: Low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening can cut the risk of dying from lung cancer by 16% in high-risk people, while also reducing the incidence of advanced stage III or IV disease, an International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) working group has found.Published in The New England Journal of Medicine, the assessment found established evidence that low-dose CT reduces lung cancer mortality when used in people at high risk based mainly on age and smoking history.IARC convened a working group of 23 clinicians and scientists from 17 countries, including Dr Abhishek Shankar of All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, to assess the benefits and harms of lung cancer screening.The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history, typically at least 20 to 30 pack-years. Studies involving former smokers generally included those who had quit within the previous 10 to 15 years, with screening usually performed annually.In India, people aged 50 to 80 with at least 20 pack-years of smoking who are current smokers or quit within the past 15 years can contact the Indian Lung Screening Trial, led by Dr Abhishek Shankar at AIIMS, New Delhi, about screening.Dr Shankar has invited eligible people to contact him for screening under the trial.The evidence behind the finding came mainly from randomised trials. In the US National Lung Screening Trial, people screened with low-dose CT had a 16% lower relative risk of dying from lung cancer than those screened with chest X-rays at seven years. The European NELSON trial also found lower lung cancer mortality among men screened with low-dose CT at 10 years.Based on this evidence, the IARC group classified low-dose CT as Group A, indicating established evidence that it reduces lung cancer mortality and the incidence of stage III or IV disease. Chest X-rays, with or without sputum examination, were classified as Group C, as their ability to reduce lung cancer mortality could not be established.However, the review cautioned that low-dose CT screening is not meant for everyone. False-positive results ranged from 1% to 42% across studies, depending on the screening protocol. Among those with false-positive results, 5% to 32% underwent at least one invasive procedure, with complications occurring in 10% to 22% of such procedures.The review also estimated that 3% to 26% of lung cancers detected in randomised trials involving high-risk people could represent overdiagnosis, meaning cancers that might not have caused harm during the person's lifetime.The working group said effective lung cancer screening needs more than CT scanners, including systems for identifying eligible people, assessing risk, monitoring nodules, providing treatment and follow-up, along with smoking-cessation support. Organised programmes also require trained staff, quality assurance, adequate healthcare capacity and equitable access.
Article Summary: Lung cancer deaths can be reduced through low-dose ct screening. It can also help detect the disease before it reaches advanced stages in people at high risk. The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history, typically at least 20 to 30 pack-years.

Article Title: No road agency, contractor penalised for death, disability due to design failures
Article Text:
Faulty road design can turn an everyday drive into a deadly crash.

NEW DELHI: Even seven years after a penal provision was introduced to hold road contractors, designers and road-owning agencies accountable for crashes caused by faulty road design, construction or maintenance resulting in death or disability of victims, not a single agency has been penalised so far under this provision of Motor Vehicles Act Last week experts flagged this issue at a conference on the impact of amendments that govt made to the Motor Vehicles Act in 2019 while pointing out the need to carry out detailed and proper investigation into all serious crashes across all types of roads. However, there have been few instances where agencies and courts have pulled up road owning entities for failure on their part for serious crashes.Only this year, govt increased the penalty for agencies found responsible in such cases by 50 times -- from earlier provision of up to Rs 1 lakh “fine” to up to Rs 50 lakh “penalty” through an amendment to Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act.While fines can be imposed by courts after trial, which is a lengthy process, penalties can be levied directly by administrative, regulatory, or governing authorities for non-compliance without a court trial. Sources said this change is likely to have its impact on govt authorities taking action against agencies responsible for poor design, construction and maintenance where these factors resulted in a serious crash.Some officials of the state road owning agencies admitted that one of the biggest hurdles is establishing a direct causal link between a road engineering defect and a crash as in almost all cases multiple reasons contribute to accidents. This has resulted in accountability remaining confined largely to drivers, with agencies responsible for planning, constructing and maintaining roads escaping scrutiny.The MV Act amendments in 2019 specified that while imposing the fine, courts must consider the road’s design, expected traffic, applicable maintenance standards, the condition in which users could reasonably expect to find the road, whether the designated authority knew or should have known about the hazardous condition, and whether adequate warning signs had been displayed.
Article Summary: Not a single agency has been penalised so far under this provision of motor vehicles act. Only this year, govt increased the penalty for agencies found responsible in such cases by 50 times. Some officials of the state road owning agencies admitted that one of the biggest hurdles is establishing a direct causal link between road engineering defect and a crash.

Article Title: Despite rainfall deficit, kharif acreage above 5-year average
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Overall acreage of kharif (summer-sown) crops in the country declined by just over 1% this year compared with last year and while the dip was expected due to deficient monsoon rainfall this year, the sowing season still ended up recording higher than 'normal' (average of last five years) acreage. Though only marginally above the 'normal', it reflects tweaks in farmers' strategy if warning comes in advance.Latest acreage data shows total sown area at 1,107 lakh hectares (ha) as of Friday was 3 lakh ha more than 'normal' acreage (1,104 lakh ha) despite a cumulative deficit of 12% (June 1-Sept 26) in monsoon rainfall. In the same period in 2025, which recorded 8% more than normal (surplus) rainfall, total acreage was 1,121 lakh ha.The most popular kharif crop and one of the most water-intensive, paddy, reported a 3.6% decline in acreage compared with last year, but this was still 4.6% higher than the 'normal' acreage. Another guzzler, sugarcane, too reported higher acreage than its normal sown area, reflecting farmers' preference for crops which assure them of better returns, even as they had to depend on excessive use of groundwater, at the risk of high input cost.The real test of what rainfall deficit will entail, however, may be reflected in the yield of these crops, first estimates for which will soon be released by the Union agriculture ministry. The output of pulses (mainly pigeon peas), oilseeds (mainly soybean and groundnut), cotton and coarse cereals (mainly bajra and maize) may be a real concern due to deficient and skewed distribution of rainfall in the 'monsoon core zone' - the large part of central India and Bihar which depend on seasonal rains for farming in absence of adequate irrigation coverage.Floods in certain parts of Bihar and Assam, and drought in parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka may also negatively impact the overall output.Apprehending the impact of deficient monsoon rainfall on the rabi (winter-sown) crops due to low moisture content in the soil and shortage of water for irrigation, the agriculture ministry will discuss contingency measures at a two-day meet starting Monday.
Article Summary: Overall acreage of kharif (summer-sown) crops in the country declined by just over 1% this year compared with last year. The dip was expected due to deficient monsoon rainfall this year. But the sowing season still ended up recording higher than 'normal' (average of last five years)

Article Title: 'Use lowest effective dose of Nsaids': Fresh advisory on kidney risks of painkiller abuse
Article Text:
Health Ministry warns against misuse of painkillers, antibiotics over kidney disease risk.

NEW DELHI: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has issued a fresh advisory on rational consumption of painkillers and antibiotics, in view of their repeated use, without proper medical advice, putting people at the risk of kidney complications and other adverse effects.The drug regulator's circular says non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (Nsaids) and antibiotics are prescription medicines under Drugs and Cosmetics Rules and should be used only when clinically indicated, at the appropriate dose and duration and under medical supervision. It has asked people not to take Nsaids, commonly used as painkillers, repeatedly or for a prolonged period without advice.Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation has also cautioned against self-medication with antibiotics and advised people with existing kidney disease or other risk factors for renal impairment to inform their doctor before taking Nsaids.Prof Sandeep Mahajan, nephrologist at AIIMS, said unregulated and prolonged use of painkillers can accelerate the decline in kidney function. "All prescription medicines should be taken under the supervision of a qualified physician, with the prescribed dose and duration strictly followed."CDSCO has advised doctors to use the lowest effective dose of Nsaids for the shortest appropriate duration, with extra caution in patients at risk of kidney injury. This comes against the backdrop of a substantial chronic kidney disease burden in India. A 2025 review of community-based studies estimated pooled chronic kidney disease prevalence at 13.24%, although estimates varied widely across regions and studies.
Article Summary: Health ministry warns against misuse of painkillers, antibiotics over kidney disease risk. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (nsaids) and antibiotics are prescription medicines. They should be used only when clinically indicated, at the appropriate dose and duration and under medical supervision.
